commentary.heading: Wall Street extends its slide before Nvidia results
commentary.body: US shares fell for a fourth straight session on Tuesday, with about 17 in every 20 S&P 500 stocks lower. The S&P 500 lost 1.03% to 7,340.5, the Nasdaq Composite eased 0.74% to 24,328.4 and the Dow dropped 849 points (1.6%). Worries about AI valuations, interest rates and tighter regulation weighed, and banks fell on concerns about a pullback in AI spending. Nvidia closed 0.4% lower, then reported quarterly revenue of US$115.8 billion and guidance above expectations after the bell; its shares rose about 2.4% in after-hours trade.

commentary.heading: Miners lead a broad ASX retreat
commentary.body: The ASX 200 fell 1.79% to 8,883.2 on Tuesday, its lowest close since late October, with 10 of 11 sectors lower. Materials slumped 3.9% as iron ore prices eased: BHP dropped 5.0%, Fortescue 5.6% and Mineral Resources 8.5%. Financials lost 1.3%, with Macquarie down 3.8% and NAB 2.8%. Utilities were the only sector to rise, up 1.5%, helped by Origin Energy and APA.

commentary.heading: Asia and Europe follow Wall Street lower
commentary.body: Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.03% to 23,508.2 as Alibaba, Tencent and Baidu were sold, Baidu after disappointing results. Mainland markets were steadier, the Shanghai Composite down 0.50% to 3,584.6 and the Shenzhen Component down 0.49% to 10,638.5. South Korea's Kospi dropped 2.6%. In London the FTSE 100 fell 1.76% to 10,689.9 as defence and technology stocks retreated.

commentary.heading: Central banks and inflation
commentary.body: There were no rate decisions on Tuesday. Minutes of the RBA's November meeting confirmed a 6–3 vote to lift the cash rate to 4.85%, with the majority pointing to persistent inflation risks. The US federal funds range remains 3.75–4.00% and the Bank of England rate 4.00%. No new CPI figures were released.

commentary.heading: Bonds, oil and the Australian dollar
commentary.body: The US 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.10% from 5.12% as investors sought safety, while the UK 10-year rose about 4 basis points to 5.39% ahead of inflation data. Australia's 10-year was around 5.14%. Brent crude rose 0.8% to about US$93.14 a barrel. The Australian dollar held near 67.4 US cents, close to its lowest level since January.

commentary.heading: What to watch
commentary.body: Today brings Australia's September-quarter wage price index, UK October inflation and, overnight, minutes from the Fed's October meeting, along with the market's reaction to Nvidia's results. Anthropic's share float is due to debut on the Nasdaq. Australian October jobs data follow on Thursday, along with Walmart and Alibaba results, and China sets its loan prime rates on Friday.
